items.title: Aviation’s Next Disaster Could Be In Your Carry-On
items.summary: Battery incidents are rising and airlines are tightening restrictions, with cabin crews the last line of defense. Is the industry doing enough to prevent the next fire, or simply getting better at putting them out?

items.title: Airbnb Sells IP to AI Lab Owned by Its CEO and CTO
items.summary: Airbnb’s CEO and CTO both own part of the lab buying its IP, but the filing gives shareholders little detail on what changed hands.

items.title: MakeMyTrip Buys Into Daily Commutes With Quick Ride Stake
items.summary: As its air business softens, MakeMyTrip is pushing harder into everything else. Quick Ride gives it a product people use on a random Thursday, not just before a holiday. The test is whether those commuters become MakeMyTrip travelers.

items.title: Tourism Heads to COP31 Wanting Results, Not More Pledges
items.summary: Five years after the Glasgow Declaration, tourism has plenty of climate commitments but little shared proof of what they’ve achieved. The industry is still split on whether better measurement or faster action should come first.

items.title: How to Plan Your Day at Skift Aviation Forum 2026
items.summary: Jet fuel above $4 a gallon has reset the math on every airline plan for 2027. Next week, the executives making those calls spend a full day at the TWA Hotel at JFK. Here is how to spend yours, by role.

items.title: Qatar’s Tourism Recovery is Coming by Road, Not Air
items.summary: Qatar’s visitor numbers are recovering on road traffic across the Saudi border, while air arrivals keep falling. Drive-in visitors tend to make shorter trips, which limits how much they can do for hotels.
